units.ticks: servo positions as reported (homing offset applied)
units.tcp_m: metres, the model's world frame: the tool point 35 mm along the approach from the gripper's tool frame
units.gap_mm: the gripper's jaw gap in millimetres

ticks_rule: ticks = the table's joint_map on rad (today zero 2048 and sign +1 on every joint: round(2048 + rad * 4096 / (2 pi))); ticks are written here for reading, the tool recomputes them
interpolation: each move is a straight line in joint space, timed by the quintic smootherstep u -> 6u^5 - 15u^4 + 10u^3 over its duration; angles are never wrapped (the pan turns the way the numbers say); the jaw gap follows the cubic smoothstep 3u^2 - 2u^3 over gap_duration_s (default the move's)

gripper.rule: ticks for a gap: the straight line through open and grasp (24.2 ticks per mm); the grasp value is the goal that closed on an object with the force limited, not a measured 53 mm

about: shoulder load test under the bench supply: folded -> travel -> look_down -> look_floor -> above the taught pose -> the low pose where the shoulder stalled

travel.check: the delivered cycle's travel pose with the roll set to 3221 (as in drive): the delivered 1601 turned the camera under the gripper on the way to the observation poses

look_down.check: REFERENCE, set with the builder on by his eye on the robot: arm base in MOSS's axis (pan 2931 -> 2865), gripper straight (roll 3261 -> 3214), gripper vertical (CAD tilt 0.7 deg), wrist camera ON TOP, pointing at the floor about 5 cm ahead of the rover's nose (the camera looks slightly backward on its mount); jaw tips 19.3 from the floor (his ruler; dictated 'mm', the CAD says 18.5 cm for the jaws: cm). Servos read [2862, 1602, 2431, 3174, 3220] under load (the shoulder sags 19 ticks). Gripper open 90 mm. Pan returns within 0.4 deg after a 90 deg swing (test ).
